Er det tid for guttetur?

Is it time for a boys’ trip?

Seven ways to say “no” became one “Ja!” The answer changed before the random index did.

View the repository
Two commits, 69 seconds apart

Yes, with an indexing problem.

The March 2021 website picked from seven responses to “Is it time for a boys’ trip?” “Nope,” “Helst ikke” and “Kanskje vente til pandemien er over?” gave a fairly consistent answer.

On 27 October, I replaced the list with “Ja!” The code still picked a position from zero to six. There was now an answer at position zero and nothing in the other six.

The next commit set the index to zero. The recorded commit times are 69 seconds apart. You can inspect the gap below; the larger recreation cycles through the March and October responses.

02Team retrospectivesAlive
Started in 2017

Retrospective.fun

Every retro remembers the last one.

A team can agree to change something, then have the same conversation a month later. Retrospective.fun keeps earlier notes and actions within reach.

Visit Retrospective.fun
Read about this project

Keeping track between meetings

I started Retrospective.fun in 2017 and still work on it. A retrospective is a meeting about how a team works. The useful part is often what people agree to do afterwards.

The application keeps those notes and actions available at the next session. Teams can group what people wrote, revisit earlier discussions and choose formats such as Sailboat or Six Thinking Hats, each with its own sequence.

03Learning to read musicAlive
Original experiment: 2023

NoteGame → NoteQuest

My daughter picked up an idea I’d left unfinished.

I got as far as notes on a staff and a choice of answers. My daughter built NoteQuest from that idea; she develops the game, and I look after the backend and hosting.

Play NoteQuest
Read about this project

From NoteGame to NoteQuest

In 2023, I started NoteGame to practise reading music. It showed a note on a staff and asked you to pick the right answer. I left it unfinished.

A few years later, my daughter took up the idea and built NoteQuest using AI-assisted development. She develops the game; I provide the backend, hosting and engineering support. You can play her version now.

FIELD NOTESNOTES ON OLDER PROJECTS
N° 001SendToChrome
2015

Getting a link onto another screen

The end result was a new browser tab. Behind it were a Windows Phone app, a Chrome extension, a web API and Google Cloud Messaging.

Follow the URL

SendToChrome dates from 2015. It paired a Windows Phone with a named Chrome browser, using a short code to connect the two.

The phone requested that code from the API. You entered it in the Chrome extension and gave the browser a name. The phone could then list its paired browsers and send a URL to one of them.

The API routed the URL through Google Cloud Messaging. The extension received the message and opened a tab. The phone never needed a direct connection to the desktop.

Source: the original SendToChrome implementation, 2015.
